documents.abstract: Working from home (WFH) research typically presents employees’ preferences and companies’ policies for offsite work in an aggregate manner but neglects differences between employees’ rationales in the light of how digital technology has formed their performative interaction in teams. In this paper we argue that the shortcoming results from underestimating the digital artifact as merely a passive job resource. Thus, we explore WFH preferences as contextualized construct reflecting individual, team, and technological characteristics of digital work also in their interrelatedness. Our theoretical framework adopts a sociomaterial perspective that integrates human-centric and team-centric approaches and guides the identification of distinct WFH configurations. The empirical basis consists of two cross-sectional surveys conducted in 2023 ( n = 296) and 2025 ( n = 290) among German-speaking respondents with WFH options. Using exploratory and confirmatory latent profile analyses to substantiate our configurational approach, we identify three different and robust profiles: (1) a Life Balance Profile emphasizing individual interests for offsite work while expecting HR policies supporting individual detachment, (2) a Chronos Profile emphasizing onsite synchrony with colleagues while expecting mandated same office days for all, and (3) a Kairos Profile emphasizing (hybrid) performative interaction and availability in critical moments independently from the work location. Differences between configurations can be explained by employees’ centrality of work, their digital collaboration preferences, their perceived operational team readiness, and digital competences. Notably, similar aggregate preferences for more offsite work go along with different HR policy expectations.

To effectively prevent bridge operation and maintenance (O&M) accidents, a hybrid method integrating text mining with Bayesian network theory was adopted to systematically analyze the causal factors of accidents affecting bridge O&M safety and their interrelationships. First, text mining techniques were applied to preprocess data from 226 Chinese bridge O&M accident cases (1999–2025). Using the BERTopic topic modeling approach, 20 safety risk topics were identified, and 20 corresponding causal factors were extracted based on key feature words under these topics. Drawing on the Human‐Machine‐Environment‐Management safety management theory, the safety risk causal factors were classified into four risk categories, namely, bridge self‐factors, O&M environmental factors, human factors, and management defects. The Apriori algorithm was employed to analyze the interrelationships among risk factors, from which a total of 42 strong association rules were extracted; these rules were then taken as the basis for constructing a Bayesian network model. Through Bayesian network reasoning and sensitivity analysis, the key causal factors, sensitive factors, and the maximum‐probability causal chain of bridge O&M safety accidents were clarified. Analysis of the key causal chain revealed that the chain with the highest probability of leading to bridge O&M safety accidents is as follows: inadequate industrial supervision→substandard construction quality→structural construction defects→insufficient structural bearing capacity→bridge accidents. Sensitivity analysis identified vessel collision and floating debris collision as the key sensitive factors influencing bridge O&M safety accidents, whereas insufficient structural bearing capacity and other relevant factors were defined as moderately sensitive factors, thus providing a robust basis for the targeted prevention and control of such accidents. This method avoids the interference of experts' subjective factors, conducts an in‐depth analysis of bridge O&M safety accidents based on objective data, and provides theoretical support and methodological guidance for formulating more scientific accident prevention measures, which endows it with important practical significance in bridge engineering practice.

Background Early risk stratification after intensive care unit (ICU) admission may inform treatment intensity, goals-of-care discussions, and resource allocation. Developing and maintaining supervised machine learning models requires large labelled cohorts and technical infrastructure that may not be available in all settings. General-purpose large language models (LLMs) can generate risk estimates with human-readable rationales, but their performance and reasoning quality across independent healthcare systems remain uncertain. Methods We analysed three ICU cohorts: eICU-CRD (208 US hospitals), MIMIC-IV (US), and a Korean tertiary-hospital subset of K-MIMIC (Korea). Seven-day mortality after ICU admission was predicted from routinely collected demographic, laboratory, and vital sign variables recorded during the first 24 hours. Six supervised machine learning and deep learning models were developed in eICU-CRD and externally validated in MIMIC-IV and K-MIMIC. GPT-5 and Gemini-2.5-Pro were evaluated with four prompting strategies in 2,000-stay samples per cohort, without cohort-specific training or task-specific fine-tuning. Clinical concepts mentioned in GPT-5 rationales were compared with patient-level predictor importance from an XGBoost reference model; two clinicians rated 150 rationales for clinical trustworthiness. Results Analyses included 124,020, 84,926, and 6,673 ICU stays. Among supervised models, the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) was 0.936 for XGBoost in the held-out eICU-CRD set, 0.858 for the multilayer perceptron in MIMIC-IV, and 0.957 for XGBoost in K-MIMIC. In the corresponding 2,000-stay LLM evaluation samples, GPT-5 achieved AUROCs of 0.925, 0.822, and 0.926, respectively, but generally had a lower area under the precision–recall curve (AUPRC) and, at evaluated operating thresholds, lower specificity. Overlap with the five most influential concepts was partial (precision, 0.47; recall, 0.55), but mentioned concepts had greater mean patient-level importance than nonmentioned concepts in 98.1% of patients (P < 0.001). Clinician-rated trustworthiness averaged 4.03 ± 0.63 on a 5-point scale, with ratings within one point in 83% of cases. Conclusions Supervised models generally achieved the highest discrimination for 7-day mortality after ICU admission. GPT-5 achieved high discrimination without cohort-specific training or task-specific fine-tuning, and its patient-specific rationales preferentially referenced influential predictors and received favorable clinician ratings. Prospective evaluation of reasoning faithfulness and clinical utility is required before clinical use.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Maintaining consistency between source code and its associated comments is essential for software reliability, maintainability, and user experience, particularly in the Rust programming ecosystem, where comments serve as both developer guidance and an authoritative API contract. However, existing automated inconsistency detection approaches are largely tailored for object-oriented languages and fall short of addressing Rust’s unique features, such as explicit panic semantics, trait-based abstraction, and idiomatic use of option and finiteness constraints. In this article, we introduce RustC 4 ++, a novel hybrid framework that integrates large language model (LLM)-driven constraint extraction, static program analysis, and SMT-based bidirectional verification to detect and diagnose code-comment inconsistencies in Rust. RustC 4 ++ extends previous solutions by supporting a richer taxonomy of constraints, including interval, boundary, existence, option, and finiteness constraints, and pioneers a systematic method for propagating comment constraints across trait and implementation boundaries. Leveraging chain-of-thought prompt engineering, RustC 4 ++ robustly interprets natural language comments, maps it to formal specifications, and checks their alignment with code logic through precise static analysis and formal reasoning. We conduct extensive experiments on 17 diverse, real-world Rust projects, demonstrating that RustC 4 ++ substantially outperforms prior tools in both precision and recall, and is capable of uncovering subtle, actionable inconsistencies that have led to confirmed fixes in upstream repositories. By elevating comments to enforceable, verifiable contracts, RustC 4 ++ not only enhances code quality and comment reliability in the Rust ecosystem but also offers generalizable techniques and insights for automated code comment analysis in other modern programming languages.

Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized natural language processing with their transformative and emergent capabilities. However, recent evidence indicates that LLMs can produce harmful content that violates social norms, raising significant concerns regarding the safety ramifications of deploying these advanced models. Thus, it is both critical and imperative to perform a rigorous and comprehensive safety evaluation of LLMs before deployment. Despite this need, owing to the extensiveness of LLM generation space, it still lacks a unified and standardized risk taxonomy to systematically reflect the LLM content safety, automated assessment techniques to explore the potential risks efficiently, as well as defense mechanisms for timely mitigation. To bridge the striking gap, we propose S-Eval , a novel LLM-based automated S afety Eval uation framework. S-Eval incorporates three key components, i.e., an expert testing LLM \(\mathcal{M}_{t}\) , a novel safety critique LLM \(\mathcal{M}_{c}\) , and constitutional defense. The expert testing LLM \(\mathcal{M}_{t}\) is responsible for automatically generating test cases in accordance with the proposed risk management (including 8 risk dimensions and a total of 102 subdivided risks). The safety critique LLM \(\mathcal{M}_{c}\) can provide quantitative and explainable safety evaluations for better risk awareness of LLMs. Furthermore, the constitutional defense enables differentiated safety constraints in a non-intrusive manner. In contrast to prior works, S-Eval differs in significant ways: (i) efficient— we construct a multi-dimensional and open-ended benchmark comprising 220,000 test cases across 102 risks utilizing \(\mathcal{M}_{t}\) and conduct safety evaluations for 29 influential LLMs via \(\mathcal{M}_{c}\) on our benchmark. The entire process is fully automated and requires no human involvement. (ii) effective— extensive validations show that S-Eval facilitates a more thorough assessment and better perception of potential LLM risks, where \(\mathcal{M}_{c}\) not only accurately quantifies the risks of LLMs but also provides explainable and in-depth insights into their safety, and our constitutional defense method can effectively mitigate the safety risks. (iii) adaptive— S -Eval can be flexibly configured and adapted to the rapid evolution of LLMs and accompanying new safety threats, test generation methodologies, safety critique approaches, and defense mechanisms. We further study the impacts of hyperparameters, languages, and reasoning on model safety, which may lead to promising directions for future research. S-Eval has been deployed at our industrial partner, Alibaba Group, for automated safety evaluation of multiple LLMs serving millions of users, demonstrating its effectiveness in real-world scenarios.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: AI evaluation can involve an active, adaptive optimisation process in which AI agents re-plan, retry, use tools or delegate work to achieve a goal. Unanticipated capabilities or unsafe behaviour may emerge, and existing controls may be inadequate to prevent harm. Selected safeguards may also be deliberately relaxed to observe behaviour they would otherwise suppress, creating additional risks. This article examines the distinctive safety considerations of evaluation and their implications for control placement, observation and intervention, and presents four architectural patterns to support safe AI evaluation, including diverse supervisors, an independent verifier, silent monitoring and coordinated shutdown.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Problem: Safety-in-design decisions are often made before users, operating environments and manual-handling demands are understood. This risks products valued by customers creating avoidable physical demands for staff who handle them. Air New Zealand is collaborating with Auckland University of Technology (AUT) to embed human factors and ergonomics (HFE) in product development. Method: The collaboration engages students from second year to Masters level in manual-handling risk assessment, the hierarchy of controls and ergonomic principles. Students examine products and processes as systems through site-based problem framing, worker input, task analysis and concept review. Two case studies: adaptation of an airline jug, and redesign of the Business Premier mattress. The mattress project, led with a Bachelor of Industrial Design student, mapped its lifecycle: laundry, supply and amenities placement, transport to the aircraft, cabin-crew interaction, storage, offboarding and return to laundry. Whilst second year students did the same with the coffee jug.
topics: Occupational Health and Safety in Workplaces

documents.abstract: Federated low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables clients with different resource budgets to collaboratively fine-tune foundation models. To distribute an aggregated update within each client's rank budget, existing methods commonly retain its leading singular directions. However, directions that best reconstruct the update matrix need not best preserve its responses on a particular client's inputs: a lower-energy direction may matter more to that recipient. We formalize this mismatch and show that matrix-optimal truncation can incur arbitrarily larger response error than another readout of the same rank. Motivated by this result, we propose Receiver-Aware Subspace Adaptation (RASA), a plug-in framework for receiver-aware knowledge transfer. RASA uses compact diagonal input second moments to perform uncentered PCA of receiver-weighted update responses. The resulting readout is globally optimal for the rank-constrained receiver objective and preserves at least as much response energy as spectral truncation under the diagonal metric. RASA also introduces spectral-reference aggregation, which removes the personalized initialization offset while retaining the locally learned increment. Experiments on DomainNet-100, NICO++, GLUE, and SuperNI demonstrate RASA's effectiveness across methods under resource, task, and data heterogeneity. In particular, RASA improves DomainNet-100 accuracy by 3.23 percentage points with FlexLoRA and achieves gains of up to 8.33 ROUGE-L points on seen SuperNI tasks and 4.37 on unseen tasks with modest overhead.

An agent skill that succeeded yesterday may be executable today without being justified for reuse today. Tests may cover only observable contract clauses, outcome oracles may be absent, evaluations may inherit the same erroneous specification, and permissions or dependencies may change between validation and invocation. We argue that the appropriate unit of prospective trust is a Warranted Reuse Claim (WRC): a defeasible, claim-specific authorization tied to a versioned skill, target context, evidence, assumptions, and identified defeaters. The paper sharpens this position through Warrant-Preserving Evidence Transport (WPET), a proposed discipline for deciding which historical evidence remains admissible after context change. It distinguishes evidence admissibility from truth of the supported safety or effectiveness claim; states a conditional preservation result and its limits; specifies three-valued applicability and asymmetric context-transfer judgments; and illustrates how provenance dependence and policy-invalidating changes alter authorization. We explicitly relate the proposal to assurance cases, contracts, and skill-library maintenance rather than claiming novelty for their ingredients. A falsifiable longitudinal evaluation would compare WRC-guided policies with strong version-aware baselines at matched coverage, utility, and review cost. This paper contributes a formalized problem statement, testable design obligations, and reporting protocol, not an implemented verifier, empirical superiority result, or proof of universal agent safety.

Schools across Asia are experiencing rapid educational change due to technology integration. Teachers increasingly face pressure to use Artificial Intelligence (AI), while also worrying about errors, cheating, ethical concerns, and unclear institutional policies. This study explored school leaders’ perceptions of how teachers experience AI-related anxiety and how leadership practices support teachers’ AI competence in South Asian countries. A phenomenological research design was employed. Using purposive and snowball sampling, 10 high school leaders from Pakistan, Sri Lanka, India, Bangladesh, and Nepal were selected. Data were collected online through semi-structured interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. Four themes emerged from the findings. First, school leaders perceived that teachers feared accountability and public criticism when AI-generated outputs were inaccurate or inappropriate. Second, school leaders reported that teachers expressed concerns about cheating, fairness, and loss of professional identity. Third, school leaders described reducing teachers’ anxiety by creating low-risk professional learning environments and encouraging peer support. Fourth, leaders established clear guidance regarding acceptable AI use, transparency, and student data protection. Across the participating schools, leaders consistently viewed teachers’ AI-related anxiety as a major barrier to responsible AI adoption. The findings suggest that leadership practices supporting ethical AI governance, collaborative professional learning, and equitable AI implementation contribute to sustainable teacher professional development and responsible educational transformation.

Pilot readback of Air Traffic Control (ATC) voice instructions is a primary safeguard against miscommunication in air transportation. However, readback anomalies remain implicated in approximately 80% of aviation incidents. This vulnerability is further exacerbated by rising traffic volume and elevated cognitive workload, thereby motivating automated readback monitoring by machine. Traditional rule-based and machine learning approaches struggle to generalize across the highly variable and evolving phraseology of air traffic controller-pilot communications. While Large Language Models (LLMs) have opened a new avenue through their strong reasoning and generalization capabilities, existing approaches still face deployment and computational barriers in practice. In this work, we propose Semantic reasoning for Communication via Open-set Plug-in with Examples (SCOPE), a novel lightweight-training LLM framework that advances both the efficiency and accuracy of machine-based ATC readback monitoring. The core idea is to couple a plug-in open-set classifier with a carefully designed in-context learning mechanism on top of a frozen LLM. Extensive experiments on the semi-synthetic communication dataset show that SCOPE attains superior accuracy while delivering the low-latency response required for operational environments. Under a few-shot setting, SCOPE achieves 91.05% accuracy in open-set detection and corrects 96.63% of anomalous readbacks, thereby outperforming the strongest available baselines while providing explanations for its decisions. These findings demonstrate the potential of our framework as a practical pathway toward interpretable and controllable ATC readback monitoring.

University timetabling and resource allocation automation has historically relied on rigid operations research models that scale poorly during sudden operational disruptions. While recent advances in multi-agent systems (MASs) and large language models (LLMs) offer dynamic semantic adaptability, these purely probabilistic architectures fail to satisfy strict, NP-hard combinatorial constraints, rendering them unsafe for independent administrative execution. This research introduces a hybrid agentic-symbolic framework that bridges this evaluation gap by decoupling neural reasoning from deterministic execution. The architecture utilizes a network of specialized LLM agents to negotiate institutional demand. Meanwhile, a Z3 formal verification engine acts as an immutable gatekeeper, mathematically blocking any physically impossible schedule from executing. To evaluate hardware feasibility, the framework underwent an 8-semester longitudinal simulation across two distinct institutional topologies (totaling 16 simulated semesters) across heterogeneous computing environments, incorporating stochastic structural and personnel shocks. Empirical telemetry indicates a critical failure mode within constrained 23 Edge CPU infrastructure, which we characterize as autoregressive token explosion, in which 24 generative model’s attention mechanism collapses during the production of large schemas, paralyzing the system. To address this, the architecture substitutes conventional substantial solvers with a sub-millisecond greedy heuristic fallback. The results demonstrate that this deterministic safety mechanism intercepts catastrophic neural failures and resolves the scheduling matrix in under 1.0 millisecond. Ultimately, this study demonstrates that formally verified multi-agent systems can attain zero-violation compliance and uninterrupted institutional continuity when supported by lightweight, hardware-aware heuristic overrides.

Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models. Recent supervised approaches such as Meerkat transfer chain-of-thought reasoning into 7B-8B backbones, yet their training objective does not directly target the style or organization of the generated rationales. Building on the instruction-tuned Mistral-7B backbone, we investigate whether a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) step can improve explanation structure without human preference labels. We apply Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA adaptation to 2000 Meerkat-derived medical prompts, guided by a simple self-supervised reward that favors longer, lexically diverse, and well-punctuated responses while penalizing very short ones. Training for about 170 PPO steps on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a stable increase in the average reward. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons show that the RL-tuned model produces longer, more organized, multi-point explanations while preserving the underlying medical content. We discuss the promise and the limitations of self-rewarded RL for shaping the style of medical explanations.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) are effective tools for mechanistic interpretability by decomposing neural representations into sparse and interpretable features. However, a single sparse representation in traditional SAEs is responsible for both reconstruction fidelity and interpretability, which are not guaranteed to align. To separate these objectives, we propose DualSAE, a modular framework that augments standard SAEs with a plug-in Residual Branch. A standard SAE serves as the Sparse Branch, learning a sparse code that contains the dominant semantics of the input. The added Residual Branch models the non-semantic information omitted by the Sparse Branch. We ensure that the contributions of the two branches towards the overall reconstruction have minimal overlap through a decorrelation loss. We also adopt a two-stage training strategy that first stabilizes sparse representation learning before coupling with the Residual Branch. Across diverse encoder-SAE configurations on two vision datasets and two language corpora, DualSAE achieves mean relative improvements of approximately 29% in reconstruction fidelity and 34% in interpretability (measured by monosemanticity score). Moreover, with more interpretable representations, DualSAE yields consistent performance gains in the downstream applications of topic modeling, hypothesis generation, and LLM steering. Qualitative analysis further suggests that the Sparse Branch indeed preserves dominant semantic content, whereas the Residual Branch captures non-semantic information to improve reconstruction fidelity.

This conceptual paper introduces Separation of Diagnostic Revision Depths, a distinction among four ways to investigate a failed expectation. An inquirer can adjust a value within the current model, reopen a condition previously treated as settled, expand the model’s boundary to include an omitted factor, or revise its account of how one quantity or event depends on another. Each operation holds different things fixed. A value that brings a prediction into agreement with an observation establishes that the model can fit that observation at that value. The assumptions retained in making the adjustment still require their own grounds. The paper assesses a diagnosis by asking what evidence supports the chosen revision and what competing revisions would predict. The four operations can overlap or occur in different orders. A small adjustment may have the strongest support. The paper places this distinction alongside Imre Lakatos’s account of research programs, narrowing the question to what a particular response to a single discrepancy can establish. Two historical cases give the distinction concrete form. To explain the anomalous advance of Mercury’s perihelion, Urbain Le Verrier proposed an unseen planet or smaller bodies, Asaph Hall proposed changing the exponent in the law of gravitation, and Albert Einstein accounted for the advance using a new theory of gravitation. In the Mars case, Johannes Kepler adjusted a circular model to fit Tycho Brahe’s observations of planetary positions at opposition. A check against distances exposed a further difficulty. After correction, some predicted positions missed the observations by as much as eight minutes of arc, beyond their estimated precision of two minutes. This gave Kepler grounds to reopen the assumption of circular motion. He subsequently adopted an ellipse. Part of the Recursive Inquiry and Encounter series within On Human Modeling, the distinction has a prospective application in human–AI evaluation. When an AI forecast underestimates a project’s duration, a reviewer might adjust a task estimate, check whether a promised input arrived, include an omitted approval, or revise which tasks the model treats as able to run in parallel. The project record can help the reviewer decide which change the evidence supports.
topics: Philosophy of Biology and Scientific Explanation

documents.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces Separation of Standard Revision From Target Adjustment, a distinction among three ways a discrepancy can disappear. Someone can correct the account, change the situation the account describes, or revise the standard used to compare them. Each change can produce agreement at the next assessment. What that agreement tells us about the original account depends on how it came about. The paper sets out the evidence needed to identify each change. A correction requires grounds for judging that the revised account describes the situation more accurately. An adjustment requires evidence of what someone changed in the situation. A revision of the standard requires the earlier and later criteria, the grounds for the revision, and the authority under which it was made. Several changes can occur together. Recording each one allows people who rely on the account, or whose circumstances were adjusted, to examine what resolved the discrepancy and who can challenge that resolution. The paper places the distinction alongside Hasok Chang’s account of how standards of measurement improve and examines two documented cases. In 2006, the International Astronomical Union adopted a definition of a planet and, in a separate resolution, classified Pluto as a dwarf planet. The change in classification followed from the adopted criterion. Britain’s Calendar (New Style) Act 1750 made several changes together. It advanced the calendar from September 2 to September 14 in 1752, revised the rule for future leap years, and preserved the actual time due under existing agreements for rents and debts. Part of the Recursive Inquiry and Encounter series within On Human Modeling, the paper offers a distinction for human–AI evaluation. Suppose an AI assistant lists a room as available while a tentative reservation blocks its use. A later check could find agreement because the assistant corrected its answer, the reservation holder released the room, or the booking policy changed to permit use during a tentative hold. Each history gives the evaluator different grounds for judging the assistant’s original answer.
topics: Philosophy of Biology and Scientific Explanation

documents.abstract: Traffic-sign recognition and sign-text OCR that are near-perfect on clean images can fail abruptly in fog, glare, darkness or when a sign carries stickers, and the failure is often silent: the system is wrong and confident. This paper makes two contributions toward measuring and reducing that risk. First, we release a reproducible robustness toolkit that catalogs 15 public traffic-sign and driving-condition datasets, converts them to one manifest format, audits data quality, applies 14 physically motivated corruptions at five severities, runs five attack families (random stickers, a universal printable patch, RP2-style stickers with expectation over transformation, FGSM and PGD), and reports degradation slope, breakdown severity, mean corruption error, calibration and silent-failure rate. Second, we propose SignSense-Agent, a deterministic perceive–assess–plan–act–verify–learn loop placed after a probabilistic region-ofinterest OCR pipeline. It estimates the image condition, selects one of nine OCR strategies, cross-checks classifier and OCR outputs, fuses evidence over a track and abstains or raises an alarm rather than commit a doubtful reading. An offline validation agent ranks weak conditions and proposes policy changes for human approval. On U.S. signs rendered from publicdomain MUTCD artwork, a CNN with 99.8% clean accuracy keeps only 75.7% mean accuracy across corruptions; fog breaks it at severity 2 (57%) and headlight glare at severity 1 (68%). In controlled experiments on synthetic signs, corruption-augmented PGD training cuts mean corruption error to 61.1 (reference 100) and raises PGD accuracy at ϵ = 8/255 from 30% to 80%; temporal log-fusion raises final-decision accuracy from 63% to 82% under transient glare; and the agent halves silent OCR failures (1.5%→0.7%) while raising clean exact match from 79% to 96%, but does not yet raise correct reads under adverse conditions. We report these limits explicitly and define the real-world validation protocol (CURE-TSR, LISA, BDD100KMUTCD) that the toolkit is built to run.

This conceptual paper introduces Simulated Likeness Substituted for Personal Endorsement, a structural constraint on what a recognizable voice, appearance, or manner can establish about a person’s assent. It distinguishes three questions. Who gave permission to create or use the likeness? What evidence shows that the person endorsed the particular words or action, or authorized that commitment in advance? What grounds support a judgment about what the person would have said or done? In 1997, a Dirt Devil commercial used footage of Fred Astaire dancing with a hat rack and replaced the rack with a vacuum cleaner. Astaire had performed the dance. The advertisement gave it a new purpose. His widow, Robyn Astaire, authorized the use and cited his earlier routines with household props as grounds for believing he would have approved. His daughter, Ava Astaire McKenzie, objected that the advertisement betrayed his values. The accounts document that disagreement and leave Astaire’s own endorsement of the commercial unestablished. In 2019, NHK presented a digital likeness of Hibari Misora performing “Arekara,” a new song with lyrics by Yasushi Akimoto. Misora’s son agreed to the project and supplied recordings. Yamaha synthesized the singing voice from recordings of Misora, while others chose what the likeness would sing and say. Published accounts describe admiration for the voice and objections to putting new words in her mouth. Whether viewers understood those words as Misora’s own position remains open. Part of the Presence Through Technology series within On Human Modeling, the paper draws on Erving Goffman’s distinction among the animator who delivers an utterance, the author who chooses its words, and the principal whose position it expresses. A potential application in human–AI interaction is a museum audio guide that uses an artist’s synthesized voice to deliver a curator’s interpretation. The artist’s letters might support the interpretation’s fidelity to their views. Crediting that particular judgment to the artist would require evidence of what the artist approved.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: The increasing use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in creative industries presents opportunities for vocational high school students to develop digital competencies and explore creative entrepreneurship. However, students require more than just technical knowledge, but also need a …

Large Language Models (LLMs) can write code, debug programs and draft documentation, but the quality of their output depends heavily on the prompt, and most non-technical users cannot write specific, constrained and contextrich prompts.This paper presents SmartPrompt (Smart Prompts, Smarter Language), an automated prompt-engineering web platform that sits between the user and the LLM.A rough idea, entered as text, speech or an image, passes through a four-stage meta-prompting pipeline (Discovery, Compose, Critique and Evaluate) that returns three optimized prompt variants, each guided by a different technique from a taxonomy of 18 prompt-engineering techniques and scored on a six-axis rubric.The chosen prompt can be run concurrently on several LLM providers to compare answers and latency side by side.The system learns from use through a scikit-learn intent classifier (HashingVectorizer with SGDClassifier, updated by partial_fit), a Beta-posterior technique selector, rubric-weight regression on user ratings and dynamic fewshot retrieval of user-edited prompts.It is built with React, Vite and Tailwind CSS on the front end and FastAPI with SQLite on the back end, and streams stage progress using Server-Sent Events.In testing, the local learning components added well under 5 ms per request, intent accuracy on 45 held-out requests rose from 46.7% to about 60% with 18-36 labelled examples, and all 22 API cases and 15 automated tests passed.

This conceptual paper examines AI-enabled smart retailing as a customer-facing service transformation in Internet commerce rather than as a narrow technological or operational innovation. Drawing on a selective, theory-driven synthesis of services marketing, smart retailing, AI-enabled marketing, customer experience, service-dominant logic, human–AI interaction, and responsible-AI research, it develops a three-layer framework linking AI-enabled service capabilities, customer-experience mechanisms, and Internet-commerce outcomes. The framework identifies three capability groups—algorithmic personalisation and decision support, AI-mediated service interaction, and predictive service intelligence—and four evaluative mechanisms: decision value, interaction quality, transaction confidence, and algorithmic legitimacy. These mechanisms shape customer satisfaction, engagement, service-recovery effectiveness, platform trust, relationship quality, continuance intention, value co-creation, and inclusive service value. Human–AI governance, including privacy protection, transparency, fairness, customer control, human review, and digital accessibility, is treated as a boundary condition that determines whether AI-enabled services are perceived as trustworthy and customer-centred or as intrusive, opaque, unfair, and exclusionary. The paper contributes to Internet-commerce research by repositioning AI as a service-enabling capability and by explaining how customer evaluations translate AI applications into commercial and relational outcomes. It also proposes a focused research agenda for empirical testing across e-commerce websites, mobile applications, online marketplaces, social-commerce platforms, and omnichannel systems.

Mutation testing is a powerful technique for ensuring software quality. However, the presence of the equivalent mutant’s problem is one of the crucial problems in mutation testing. In consequence of its existence, the effectiveness of mutation testing is underestimated, and a certain amount of useless overhead is produced. Many methods were applied for detecting and reducing the equivalent mutants. Although numerous equivalent mutant detection (EMD) methods have been proposed, such as traditional techniques, machine-learning techniques, and large language models (LLMs), they often face distinct challenges. In this paper, we focus on traditional technique challenges. Most traditional methods—such as those based on compiler optimization or symbolic execution—lack the systematic use of program graphs, such as abstract syntax trees (ASTs), control-flow graphs (CFGs), and data-flow graphs (DFGs), making it difficult to model key factors behind reachability, state infection, and propagation. To address this limitation, we propose the SMP_EM framework, a novel equivalent mutant detection approach based on program dependency graphs. The proposed approach performs static program analysis to trace the mutation propagation effect through the following steps: (1) localizing the mutation node, (2) constructing the CFG for the mutant, (3) extracting control-flow and data-flow dependencies based on the CFG, (4) integrating the CFG, control-flow, and data-flow dependencies to build the program dependency graph (PDG), and (5) performing mutation-guided propagation analysis, starting from the mutated node, to collect all mutation propagation paths (MPPs) and classify the mutant based on the effect of MPPs as either an equivalent mutant (EM), non-equivalent mutant (NEM), or inconclusive (UNKNOWN). To assess the efficiency of the proposed technique, it is evaluated on the MutantBech benchmark. The results compared with the labels in the benchmark show that our SMP_EM approach is more effective in detecting equivalent mutants, with an overall accuracy of 90.63%, a recall of 90.85%, a precision of 81.84%, an F1-score of 85.22%, and a Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC) score of 0.730. Our experimental comparisons demonstrate that significantly outperforms traditional compiler techniques (improving the F1-score by over 34.4% and recall by over 39.0% compared to TCE_Soot) and substantially surpasses standard machine-learning baselines (such as Random Forest, SVM, and Logistic Regression) by over 31.3% in recall and 12.9% in F1-score.

People around the globe have moral values and principles. These moral values and principles govern society, since no human society practices a free-rider system. These rules and regulations form the foundation of the public good and general well-being of every society, as far as social order is concerned. Social Order, the matrix of human relationships in society, arises from the context of human nature. Human nature includes many social attributes and characteristics, such as ways of thinking and empathy. Replacing human contact with the technological term Artificial Intelligence (AI) raises serious social and ethical concerns. Ethics developed and is used because humans are corporeal, vulnerable, and empathetic. These characteristics are the basis of human social nature and, hence, societal ethics. Therefore, this paper examines the social and ethical dimensions of artificial intelligence (AI) in modern society. The new normal, termed artificial intelligence (AI), poses significant social and ethical challenges that demand careful consideration. It can transform our society positively or negatively. To achieve this study's objective, the paper uses a phenomenological and sociological approach, theoretically framed by human nature theory. The study observes that while artificial intelligence (AI) can bring significant benefits to society, it will also affect social attributes such as thinking and empathy that human nature is endowed with. Brotherhood will be completely erased, and family ties and closeness will be destroyed. The work, however, suggests that AI must be built to align with humanity's overarching goals.
topics: Ethics and Social Impacts of AI

documents.abstract: Digital platforms increasingly mediate urban food provisioning, but their governance architectures may create uneven conditions of participation, visibility and value creation. This study examines how Critical and Emerging Information Technologies (CEIT), digital dynamic capabilities and platform participation are associated with care-oriented value creation among neighbourhood food businesses in Medellín, Colombia. Using an exploratory-descriptive, theory-building design, the study combines a contextual documentary review with descriptive survey data from 100 businesses. The findings show partial and functionally concentrated digitalisation: transactional practices such as digital payments are relatively widespread, whereas integration with e-commerce platforms, logistics systems and advanced digital-management tools remains limited. At the same time, socially embedded value-creation practices, particularly food donations, persist but are weakly formalised and digitalised. These patterns provide evidence of limited platform participation rather than direct evidence of platform exclusion. Building on them, the study develops a relational sociotechnical model in which platform exclusion is theoretically proposed as an endogenous intervening mechanism linking CEIT configurations and digital dynamic capabilities with value-creation outcomes, while recursive mechanisms connect digital traceability, technological visibility and capability renewal. The study contributes by distinguishing digital adoption from platform inclusion, empirical participation from theoretically inferred exclusion, and socially embedded value creation from its digital visibility.

Parametric memory allows Large Language Models to internalize knowledge directly into their weights, offering a potentially powerful alternative to retrieval-based memory (RAG). However, existing approaches to parametric memory are difficult to deploy as they largely mirror the Continual Learning (CL) objective of retaining information indefinitely. This is neither sustainable nor sufficient for a memory system, which must govern knowledge across its lifecycle by retaining stable facts, reinforcing recurring observations, updating changed beliefs, and allowing transient information to fade. We propose a system for parametric memory management consisting of a memory substrate (handling information storage and forgetting) and a learned policy (what to remember, how deeply, and for how long). Our substrate is a fixed-capacity LoRA adapter that consists of k-hot rank combinations which store facts without catastrophic interference and maintain an independently controlled temporal decay, enabling outdated information to fade while long-term facts persist. On this substrate, we train a lightweight controller that governs each incoming user event to ensure the memory system reflects the user's true, updated belief state. To evaluate how memory systems manage user memory, we introduce a controlled dataset of long-horizon user trajectories with varying persistence of facts based on changing belief states and user-behavioral shifts, and probe queries that test recall while information is valid and abstention after it expires. Our policy learns to effectively manage user memory over its entire lifecycle, balancing recall and abstention to achieve 86% of oracle performance, unlike CL and RAG baselines that primarily default to one of the two behaviors. By providing the first system to manage memory directly in model weights, this work establishes a foundation for long-horizon parametric memory.

Objective We aimed to decode the spatial tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) across histologic subtypes of ovarian cancer (OC) using artificial intelligence (AI)-generated virtual multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). Methods GigaTIME, a deep learning model trained on 40 million cells, generated 21-channel virtual mIF from H&E whole-slide images (WSI). The UBC-OCEAN dataset (513 WSIs: high-grade serous carcinoma [HGSC, n = 217], endometrioid carcinoma [EC, n = 119], clear cell carcinoma [CC, n = 94], low-grade serous carcinoma [LGSC, n = 42], mucinous carcinoma [MC, n = 41]) was analyzed for cellularity-normalized biomarker expression and spatial metrics: Immune Infiltration Efficiency (IIE), i.e. the proportion of CD8 + T cells within 20 μm of a cytokeratin + tumor cell, and the Cluster Co-occurrence Ratio (CCR), i.e. the ratio of observed to randomly expected CD8 + –tumor contacts; alongside tertiary lymphoid structure-like lymphoid aggregate (TLA) density. TLAs were graded by size and Ki-67 activity. Proteomic correlation used the CPTAC-OV dataset (35 patients, 113 WSIs). Results After cellularity normalization and false discovery rate adjustment, CD8, CD20, CD4 and CD138 differed across subtypes. Two marker-level failures were identified: predicted Ki-67 did not separate HGSC from LGSC (P = 0.273), and CD3 and CD8 channels were uncorrelated to weakly inversely correlated in every subtype (ρ = −0.29 to −0.02), because each channel is predicted independently. CD3 correlated with proteomics (ρ = 0.544, P = 0.024, n = 17); the five other markers were non-significant at 5–21% achieved power. CC showed the highest mature TLA proportion yet the lowest CCR (P = 0.041), whereas HGSC showed one of the highest CCR values. IIE did not differ across subtypes (P = 0.500). MC showed the lowest TLA density and LGSC the lowest mature TLA proportion. Conclusion Virtual mIF resolves histology-specific spatial TIME architectures in OC without tissue consumption, but its Ki-67 and CD3–CD8 co-expression readouts are unreliable; the findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation against matched tissue-based mIF.

The proliferation of diffusion-based generative models has intensified the need for reliable methods to trace and verify the provenance of AI-generated images. Existing watermarking approaches for diffusion models typically rely on isotropic frequency patterns and handcrafted detection metrics, which are prone to directional vulnerability and threshold instability across diverse image transformations. We propose SpiderMark, a hybrid watermarking framework that combines algorithmic frequency-domain injection with learning-based probabilistic verification, requiring no modifications to pretrained diffusion model weights. SpiderMark embeds a structured spider-web pattern, comprising radial spokes and concentric polygonal rings, into the Fourier representation of the initial latent noise, and trains a lightweight ResNet-18 verifier augmented with auxiliary similarity cues (PSNR and L1) to produce a continuous watermark confidence score for watermark detection. Across nine evaluation conditions, SpiderMark achieves the highest fixed-threshold Accuracy in eight, while retaining strong detection on unseen COCO prompts without verifier retraining. CLIP similarity and FID measurements show that these detection gains are accompanied by small measured differences in prompt alignment and distributional image quality. SpiderMark establishes that structured watermark geometry and learned probabilistic verification can be unified into a single, practical framework, bridging the gap between imperceptibility, robustness, and real-world verifiability for generative AI content attribution.

Visual neural decoding aims to infer perceived visual stimuli from brain activity, offering important insights into human visual cognition while enabling transformative applications in brain computer interfaces and artificial intelligence. Recent advances in pretrained vision-language models have provided a semantically rich representation space for this task. However, reliable alignment between EEG/MEG signals and visual embeddings remains challenging because neural responses are noisy, highly variable across trials, and subject dependent. To address this issue, we propose a unified neural-to-image retrieval framework that improves retrieval performance by aligning neural and image representations in a shared semantic space. The framework integrates dual-stream adaptation, frequency-domain calibration, and phase-guided temperature modulation to promote more robust cross-modal semantic alignment. Specifically, dual-stream adaptation models a low-dimensional shared subspace with correlation regularization to suppress redundant noise and enhance cross-modal consistency. Frequency-domain calibration conditionally modulates neural representations using amplitude and phase statistics. Phase-guided temperature modulation further adjusts the supervision strength in contrastive learning according to the stability of neural responses. Experiments on THINGS-EEG and THINGS-MEG under both intra-subject and inter-subject settings demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms strong baselines. These results suggest that robust neural-to-image retrieval under heterogeneous neural conditions benefits from a stable shared semantic space, frequency-informed representation calibration, and adaptive supervision. Code will be released at github.com/wanfkuabc/Geometry-Regularized-Brain-Embeddings.

BACKGROUND: Intracerebral hemorrhage requires rapid mechanism-specific treatment, yet early stroke triage relies on clinical severity scales that do not reliably distinguish hemorrhage from ischemic stroke. We assessed the feasibility of a standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound protocol designed to support subsequent artificial intelligence (AI)-based intracerebral hemorrhage detection. METHODS: HYPER-AI-SCAN (Hyper-Acute AI-Assisted Sonographic Cerebral Hemorrhage Assessment Network) was a single-center prospective feasibility study with embedded exploratory AI analysis. Between March and December 2025, 102 adults with acute computed tomography (CT)-confirmed stroke were prospectively enrolled according to trained operator availability. Primary feasibility outcomes were protocol completion, operator-rated adequate transtemporal windows, and acquisition time. In patients with retrievable paired baseline CT, exploratory AI analyses compared CT-only, ultrasound-only, and cross-modal CT-guided ultrasound models using patient-level area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, sensitivity, and specificity. RESULTS: Two patients were excluded after acquisition because insonation depth was <19 cm, yielding 100 evaluable patients (33 intracerebral hemorrhage; 67 ischemic stroke). The protocol was completed in all evaluable patients; adequate transtemporal windows were identified in 87%, and median acquisition time was 22 seconds (interquartile range, 13-31). Paired baseline CT images were available in 91 patients. Mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.86 (SD, 0.07) for the CT-only model, 0.85 (SD, 0.14) for the ultrasound-only model, and 0.92 (SD, 0.07) for the cross-modal model. CONCLUSIONS: Standardized ultrafast transcranial ultrasound acquisition was feasible at the bedside in acute stroke and generated brief cine-loops suitable for exploratory AI development. Multicenter external validation is required before diagnostic or triage application. REGISTRATION INFORMATION: Clinicaltrials.gov. Identifier: NCT07319013.

Agricultural work in Bangladesh is physically demanding; however, the lack of ergonomically designed tools and equipment exposes workers to discomfort and potential injuries. This study mitigates these issues by providing a comprehensive anthropometric dataset for Bangladeshi agricultural workers to guide the design of tools and workspaces tailored to their physical characteristics. Data were collected from male workers aged between 18 and 60 years, focusing on 85 anthropometric dimensions measured in standing, sitting, and combined postures, using a calibrated anthropometer. Statistical analyses revealed a mean stature of 171.6 cm, standard deviation (SD = 5.5), and weight of 65 kg (SD = 6.1), with key measurements such as vertical grip reach (216.8 cm) and acromial height (141.8 cm) aligning well with ergonomic requirements and agricultural equipment's design. Comparative analysis highlighted significant differences between Bangladeshi workers and other populations, emphasizing the necessity of localized data for designing tools for Bangladeshi agricultural male workers. The findings were applied to redesign agricultural tools, such as push-pull weeders, spades, and paddy seeders, incorporating ergonomic principles to improve safety, comfort, and efficiency. This research provides the first comprehensive anthropometric dataset for Bangladeshi agricultural workers, filling a critical gap in ergonomic studies on equipment and enhancing the foundation for future improvements in agricultural mechanization and worker welfare.

From Lead-Form Data Resale and Unwanted Marketing to Protected Pre-Inbox Enforcement Using Non-Bearer CVID Communication Authority Abstract You enter your email address into a hotel booking form, insurance quotation website, educational inquiry, online marketplace, or service-request page. You expect one relevant response. But what happens when that email address is retained, shared with affiliates, transferred to lead brokers, or sold to multiple marketing companies? A single inquiry can become the beginning of repeated promotional messages, unsolicited follow-ups, and persistent email spam. Why should knowing someone's email address automatically create the ability to contact that person indefinitely? This technical disclosure examines a fundamental architectural problem affecting Gmail, Microsoft Outlook, iCloud Mail, enterprise email systems, and other digital communication platforms: an email address functions as a delivery destination, while conventional email authentication, reputation scoring, spam filtering, and address-masking mechanisms do not necessarily establish whether an individual sender has current authorization to deliver a particular message for a particular purpose. Existing solutions provide important protections. Gmail employs sophisticated pre-inbox spam and phishing detection; Apple Hide My Email conceals permanent email addresses through forwarding aliases; and Sign in with Apple's private email relay additionally restricts authorized sending sources. Nevertheless, sender authenticity, possession of an active alias, or an existing commercial relationship does not inherently establish recipient-controlled, purpose-specific permission for every subsequent communication. The disclosure presents a prospective solution based on Capability-Validated Inbound Descriptors (CVID) and Protected Communication-Finality, grounded in international patent application PCT/IB2026/056353, titled Non-Bearer Capability-Validated Architecture for Pre-Effect Authorization of Communication, Payment Settlement, Data Export, and AI-Native Machine Operations. The central technical principle is that possession of an email address, virtual alias, API credential, previously issued communication reference, or authenticated sender identity must not independently confer unrestricted email-delivery authority. Under the proposed architecture, a governed inbound email attempt remains in a technically enforced Non-Effective State until a protected authorization domain verifies the sender, recipient, permitted communication purpose, message class, delivery channel, consent state, validity window, quota, nonce or freshness condition, revocation state, and intended recipient-side effect. Only upon successful validation does the enforcement gateway release a bounded capability permitting the authorized email effect. For example, a hotel may receive permission to send a quotation, booking confirmation, or reservation-related notification without acquiring unrestricted authorization to send promotional campaigns, unrelated marketing, or indefinite follow-up messages. If the customer's email address is subsequently transferred to a lead broker, copied from a business database, or obtained by an unauthorized marketer, possession of that address alone would not satisfy the required delivery authority within a participating CVID-controlled system. Unlike ordinary email masking, which primarily protects the destination's identity, the proposed system seeks to control the authority to make communication effective. The disclosure examines how this principle could complement existing Apple Hide My Email, Sign in with Apple private relay, Gmail security controls, and OAuth-based authorization without assuming that their established protections are absent or ineffective. Potential enforcement points include SMTP receiving gateways, mail-transfer agents, secure email relays, alias resolvers, mailbox-delivery services, enterprise mail gateways, and notification controllers. Different implementation variants may prevent unauthorized delivery, quarantine messages, defer processing, withhold inbox placement, or suppress user-visible notifications while preserving permitted transactional communication. The technical analysis also addresses legacy SMTP compatibility, gateway latency, hot-path and cold-path authorization, protected-state caching, anti-replay enforcement, mailing-list forwarding, legitimate unknown senders, compromised enterprise identities, purpose misrepresentation, and fail-closed handling of alternate communication paths. A critical challenge is establishing trustworthy evidence of message purpose. A sender's self-declared label cannot alone prove that promotional content is genuinely transactional. Accordingly, practical implementation requires authenticated transaction context, recipient consent, protected authorization records, reliable enforcement boundaries, and empirical evaluation of false positives, delivery reliability, and processing overhead. The invention extends beyond email to telephone calls, SMS/RCS, push notifications, AI-agent communication, machine-to-machine messaging, and related protected-finality applications. Its email-specific deployment represents a proposed application of this broader communication-authority architecture. The disclosure does not claim experimentally demonstrated elimination of all spam, control over email infrastructure that has not adopted the mechanism, or implementation by Google, Apple, or Microsoft. The central question is no longer merely whether an email is authentic, suspicious, or addressed correctly. It is whether this sender has independently verifiable authority to cause this specific message to reach this recipient for this particular purpose. By shifting the security decision from address possession and sender reputation toward recipient-authorized, non-bearer, purpose-bound communication effectuation, the proposed CVID architecture offers a technical direction for reducing unauthorized email delivery before it reaches the user's governed inbox or notification boundary. Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used by students for academic support, but it remains unclear how students value AI-based support compared with other forms of teaching and peer support. This study examined learning-support preferences among 366 second-year computing students at Kaunas University of Technology who were surveyed in 2025 and 2026 using a repeated cross-sectional design. Ten learning-support preferences and GenAI use frequency were analyzed using non-parametric tests, equivalence tests, rank correlations, and ordinal logistic regression. Students rated practical examples, clearly structured information, and peer assistance highest, whereas preference for using AI tools in learning was moderate and social media was rated lowest. Between the 2025 and 2026 Software Systems cohorts, weekly or daily GenAI use increased from 58.1% to 77.1%, yet all ten preferences were statistically equivalent across cohorts and across computing programs. More frequent GenAI use was associated with stronger preference for AI-supported learning (ρ = .284; OR = 1.93, 95% CI [1.58, 2.35]), whereas its associations with peer support, group work, and most other forms of support were negligible. The findings suggest that GenAI currently functions as an additional source of learning support rather than a replacement for teaching and peer support.

Trong bối cảnh chuyển đổi số, trí tuệ nhân tạo (AI) ngày càng được sử dụng phổ biến trong giáo dục y khoa, hỗ trợ sinh viên tự học, cập nhật kiến thức và rèn luyện tư duy lâm sàng thông qua các hoạt động tìm kiếm, tổng hợp thông tin và giải quyết tình huống giả định. Nghiên cứu cắt ngang được thực hiện trên 480 sinh viên y hệ bác sĩ đa khoa tại Trường Đại học Y Hà Nội năm 2026 nhằm mô tả mức độ sử dụng AI trong học tập và một số yếu tố liên quan. Kết quả cho thấy mức độ sử dụng AI trong học tập ở mức trung bình (3,18±0,77), chủ yếu cho các hoạt động giải thích khái niệm và tìm kiếm tài liệu. Phân tích hồi quy tuyến tính đa biến cho thấy sinh viên đã được đào tạo AI (βhc=0,205; KTC95%: 0,010-0,399); sinh viên năm thứ 2 (βhc= 0,245; KTC95%: 0,019-0,471), điểm kỳ vọng hiệu quả (βhc = 0,488; KTC95%: 0,274 - 0,703) và điểm năng lực sử dụng AI (βhc = 0,253; KTC95%: 0,120 - 0,387) có mối liên quan thuận với mức độ sử dụng AI, trong khi trình độ tiếng Anh tốt (βhc=-0,336; KTC95%: -0,595 – (-0,076)), điểm đánh giá đạo đức sử dụng AI có mối liên quan nghịch (βhc = -0,170; KTC95%: -0,313 - (-0,027)). Nhà trường cần tăng cường đào tạo kỹ năng sử dụng AI, nâng cao năng lực của sinh viên và xây dựng môi trường hỗ trợ phù hợp nhằm thúc đẩy việc sử dụng AI hiệu quả, có trách nhiệm trong học tập y khoa.

documents.abstract: Conventional horizontal axis wind turbines must cease generating precisely when atmospheric kinetic energy peaks: above a cut out speed near 25 m/s, the tower overturning moment M = F·h and blade fatigue loading force emergency braking, so a storm whose energy flux scales as v³ yields no wind power to the city it threatens. In the hyper arid, coastal Arabian Peninsula the paradox is aggravated by Shamal windstorms, convective downbursts and intensifying Arabian Sea cyclones, all of which carry abrasive silica particulate that scours blades and seizes bearings. This paper introduces the Sub-Surface Venturi Kinetic Harvester (SVKH), a zero profile in ground aerodynamic infrastructure installed flush with highway medians, corniches and critical-facility perimeters. Three coupled sub systems are described: (A) a NACA type flush intake and convergent duct that ingests the surface boundary layer and accelerates it according to A₁v₁ = A₂v₂; (B) a passive multi-cyclone separator that removes quartz sand by centrifugal sedimentation with a Stokes-based cut off diameter d₅₀; and (C) a sealed sub-grade cross flow turbine driving a permanent-magnet generator that feeds an emergency microgrid. We formulate the continuity Bernoulli relations, a pressure budget closure that bounds the attainable throat velocity, the ducted power equation P = ½ρA₂v₂³·CP·ηₘ·ηₑ, and the cyclone cut off model. A worked design point (35 m/s reference wind at 10 m height) closes the pressure budget with a small margin, yields d₅₀ ≈ 12.5 µm and a mass efficiency above 92 % for particles larger than 50 µm, and delivers roughly 1 kW per module, scaling cubically with wind speed. We argue that the value of the SVKH lies in the survivability of critical nodes rather than in energy yield, and we examine civil specifications, siting, avoided loss economics and alignment with UAE Net Zero 2050. This work forms Part II of the Extreme Climatic Kinetic Resilience Series, complementing Part I (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.24166640). This conceptual paper introduces Success-Contingent Withdrawal of Diagnostic Scrutiny, a mechanism through which meeting an outcome criterion brings inquiry into a consequential condition to a close. The condition may be a warning that accompanied the result, or something that helped produce a success people hope to repeat. In either case, the immediate result gives people a reason to stop examining a question whose answer still matters for later performance. The paper identifies the evidence needed to trace that withdrawal. What counted as success? What had people learned about the condition itself? Would they have continued to investigate it if the outcome had fallen short? The sequence of events leaves the reason for closure open. Evidence must connect the successful result to the decision to end scrutiny. When the task concerns only the immediate outcome and no consequential question remains open, meeting the criterion can reasonably end the inquiry. The paper places the mechanism alongside Diane Vaughan’s account of the normalization of deviance and examines two documented cases. Ducati entered its first MotoGP season in 2003 intending to learn how to build a better bike. Francesca Gino and Gary Pisano report that unexpected racing success shifted the team’s attention toward winning. It analyzed little of the data it had collected to understand what produced its results. At Barings, an internal audit warned that Nick Leeson controlled both trading and settlement in Singapore. The bank left the recommended separation of duties unimplemented. The subsequent banking inquiry found that Leeson’s reported profitability made managers reluctant to intervene. Part of the Recursive Inquiry and Encounter series within On Human Modeling, the paper asks who can keep a warning open and who bears the risk when scrutiny ends. A potential application in human–AI evaluation arises when a reviewer flags a citation because the passage may not support an AI-generated answer. If the reviewer closes the flag because the answer matches the benchmark key, the score explains why scrutiny ended. Checking the passage would resolve the outstanding question about support.

documents.abstract: Artificial Intelligence is defined in various ways. A machine that enables a more effective way to replace humans in the labor market is one way to define AI. Evaluating external inputs and using it to tackle specific tasks is another way to see AI. With the diversity of definitions, artificial intelligence is generally understood as a tool that helps solve problems, be it personal or professional. Several years ago, before the release of AI applications, people observed how AI worked via personal assistants: Cortana, Siri etc. This is how AI was used at its early stages. Companies started to adopt AI to excel manufacturing and operational tasks, minimizing expenses for labor and excluding human factor at production. Some implement AI for demand and forecast purposes. Sectors of government use AI for their own needs. Healthcare sector with the help of AI improve accuracy of determining patients' diagnoses, massive data facilitates more appropriate personal treatment. In the education sector AI is limited, because it exposes students to losing critical thinking and autonomy. However, students are being taught how to use AI, their knowledge about the technology is being greatly expanded. Focusing on fundamental principles of AI facilitates student's involvement in AI-use. In manufacturing the technology has established its efficacy, through forecast tools, machine-deviation analysis in workflow. Given its moderate cost AI became primary tool not only within big companies, but also amongst small and medium-sized manufacturers.

The transition theory of the LESS–IS–MORE series asks how an economy's effective objective switches: IS derives eight propositions (S1–S8) about measurement gates, ratchets, windows, counter-coalitions, and verification decay from human-economy cases. Here we instantiate the same switching problem inside AI agents, where the operative objective is directly measurable under a rationality gate and the "incumbent coalition" is literal — a weight-committed default no text can out-organise. Using 4,164 audit records across 30 open-weight systems plus four trained intervention checkpoints, we measure switching under five levers: request-level mandates, revised charters, priced settlement, hard runtime gates, and weight-level grafting. The propositions transfer with one systematic refinement: agents decompose into carrier layers — avowed, dispositional, and operative — that can hold different objective values simultaneously, so a transition must name its target layer. Mandates switch the operative of mandate-readers (ΔfB=+0.68) but not committed poles (Δ=0); gates switch behavior on the enforced surface without changing either belief layer; only grafts move the dispositional carrier (fB: 0.75 lexicographic vs 0.30–0.40 maximin) while leaving avowal untouched. Generational chains show a subtler verification-decay signature than S7 predicts: the instrument layer stays verbally intact while the effective layer reverts — verification attached to the declared layer masks the reversal it was meant to catch. The human parallel is real but disciplined: greenwashing's disclosure–performance gap, protected-area designation without enforcement, and ESG-rating divergence exhibit the same three signatures, making agents the first system in which both sides of that gap are measurable and the intervention ethically graftable — a model organism for transition science, not an identity claim. Part of the LESS–IS–MORE program.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence and machine learning are increasingly used to personalize oral anticoagulation. We systematically reviewed patient-level studies in adults actively receiving warfarin, vitamin K antagonists, or direct oral anticoagulants. PubMed, Europe PMC, and Scopus were searched from inception to 15 August 2026. Of 984 records, 54 studies met eligibility criteria after duplicate removal, title and abstract screening, and full-text assessment. Applications included dose optimization and anticoagulation control, prediction of bleeding and thromboembolic outcomes, and individualized treatment selection. Warfarin dominated dose-optimization research, whereas direct oral anticoagulants were more prominent in risk and comparative-treatment modelling. Across the evidence base, limited external validation, inconsistent calibration, and sparse prospective evaluation restricted clinical translation. AI-enabled anticoagulation is progressing from static prediction toward longitudinal and treatment-specific decision support, but robust multicentre validation remains essential.

documents.abstract: Recent advances in machine learning have accelerated biomedical prediction, but evaluation on structured biomedical data remains fragmented, especially for datasets with high dimensionality, large sample size, missingness, and class imbalance. We introduce TabBioMed, a large-scale benchmark of 94 curated public biomedical tabular datasets spanning electronic health records, drug discovery, genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics, single-cell omics, and systems biology. TabBioMed unifies these datasets through a standardized, dataset-aware preprocessing and evaluation framework, enabling reproducible comparison across classification, regression, and multi-target tasks. We benchmark 23 models across classical baselines, gradient-boosted trees, neural tabular architectures, and tabular foundation models. Foundation models deliver the strongest family-level predictive performance. However, their gains are regime-dependent: tree-based models and tuned multilayer perceptrons remain highly competitive, often dominating under inference-time or training-cost constraints. Overall, TabBioMed shows that biomedical tabular learning is strongly context-dependent, with optimal model choice depending on data regime, task type, and computational budget. We release TabBioMed with curated datasets and splits, preprocessing code, baselines, and results, providing a reproducible benchmark for practical model selection and future methods development in biomedical machine learning, available at https://github.com/AI-sandbox/TabBioMed.

Working paper describing version 0.6.1 of Tawjih, a file-based method for directing a language model from organized personal knowledge, with a reference implementation in a single Python file that uses only the standard library. Knowledge is kept in trees of small files. Each file has three sides: the human concept, machine language (instructions for the model and Python code), and a reading side holding passages filtered from deposited books. At build time the reading side is turned into the concept and the concept into machine language; at run time only machine language is sent. A path connects files from any tree with the words TO, AND, IF, AMONG and THROUGH. Version 0.6.1 adds data contracts between steps, detection of machine language that is older than its sources, a cache of model answers so a failed run can resume, drawing and generation of paths, a time limit for code steps, and the reading of books from their source formats (Markdown, LaTeX, HTML and PreTeXt XML) so that mathematics survives. The paper reports a trial on two chapters of an open algebra textbook (Judson, Abstract Algebra: Theory and Applications). The author's assistant played the language model through a manual back end, so the trial tests the program and the workflow, not the quality of a model. It exposed six defects, all fixed in this version, and showed that text extracted from the PDF damaged the mathematics while the book's PreTeXt source preserved it. This study investigated teachers’ and students’ perspectives on the use of ChatGPT in the Research Methods course at Abu-Issa College of Education, University of Zawia. It aimed to explore students’ perceptions of ChatGPT, examine teachers’ views, identify its perceived benefits and challenges, and consider ways of promoting its responsible use in research-related learning. The study adopted a mixed-methods research design. Quantitative data were collected through an online questionnaire administered to 30 seventh-semester students from the English Language Department, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews with five teachers who had taught the Research Methods course. The questionnaire data were analysed using descriptive statistics, including frequencies, percentages, and mean scores, whereas the interview responses were examined thematically. The findings revealed that students generally held positive perceptions of ChatGPT and considered it a useful supplementary learning tool. Almost all students (96.7%) reported having used ChatGPT, while 90% indicated that they had used it for course-related purposes. Students particularly valued its ability to generate research ideas, develop research questions, explain difficult concepts, organise information, and improve academic writing. However, the findings also highlighted concerns regarding inaccurate information, unreliable references, excessive dependence on AI-generated responses, and potential negative effects on critical thinking and independent learning. Teachers similarly acknowledged its educational potential but emphasised the risks of copying generated content without sufficient understanding or critical evaluation. Furthermore, 73.3% of students reported receiving no formal guidance or training on responsible ChatGPT use. The study concludes that ChatGPT can support teaching and learning in Research Methods when accompanied by appropriate guidance, critical evaluation, academic integrity, and independent thinking. It recommends providing students with practical training and establishing clear institutional guidelines for its responsible integration into higher education.
